technique: repetition with a difference — a word or shape returning changed
lesson:
Today we work on one thing: repetition with a difference. That means a word or a small action comes back, but something about it has changed by the second time.

This poem does it with feet. First one foot moves: "the heel finds the cold board." Later the second foot moves: "set the other foot down beside the first." One foot, then both. The action returns, but now it is finished. You also hear "cold board" twice in one line: "finds the cold board and the cold board answers." The same words come back right away, and the second time the board does something.

It works because when you hear a thing again, you measure it against the first time. The small change tells you time has passed and a decision got made.

Try this: write one small action, then bring it back later with one thing different.

The second time through, listen for the two feet, then "So — up!"

Here is the poem.
poem:
The body surfaces first, a slow tide coming in—
breath, then the heft of you settling back into your bones,
the warm dark under the quilt where you'd stay if you could.
But the heel finds the cold board and the cold board answers,
and something in you that keeps its own ledger stirs,
counting the small debts the day's already owed:
a bed of stone that waits for its three layers,
a fistful of seed measured careful against taking over,
the way a thing planted now flowers in a month you can't see yet.
You lie there one breath more, honest about the warmth,
then set the other foot down beside the first.

The dirt's still waiting for the hands that know it,
and good work only starts when you do.

So — up!
